title: Rooks That Do Not Attack Each Other

concept.title: For every row: leave it empty, or put the rook in a free column
body: Rooks attack along rows and columns. To place `k` rooks that do not attack each other, no two may share a row or a column. Go through the rows from the top. In each row there are two kinds of choices: **no rook in this row**, or **a rook in some column** that is allowed (the square is not forbidden) and not used by an earlier rook. A table `cols` remembers the used columns.

The line `if row == n: return 0` is the base case for "failure". Note that a placement is **complete** as soon as `k` reaches 0, so the rest of the board is not even visited. If fewer rows remain than rooks still to place, the branch could be cut earlier; adding the check `n - row < k` is a good pruning.

statement: A board has `n` rows and `n` columns; some squares are forbidden (`#`), the others are free (`.`). Count the ways to place exactly `k` rooks on free squares so that no two rooks are in the same row or in the same column. Two placements are different if the sets of squares are different.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has `n` characters, `.` or `#`.

examples.note: The two rooks are on a diagonal; there are 2 diagonals.

hints: For each row decide: no rook, or a rook in an allowed column that is not used.
Remember the used columns in a table and clear the entry after the recursive call.
Stop with the answer 1 as soon as all k rooks are placed.

explanation: Row by row, either no rook is placed or a rook goes to a free square in an unused column. The count of placements is returned when `k` rooks are placed; a branch with too few rows left is cut.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of partial placements (at most about 10^5 here), space O(n).
